methods.text: Write the three questions a user will ask, and answer each one on the page.
Build the worst version on purpose, then list what made it bad.
Change one thing between versions and record the effect.
Read the work aloud and cut every line you stumble on.
Give every part a weight in bytes or seconds and cut the heaviest first.
Show it for three seconds to three people, and fix what they could not describe.
Keep a log of every decision with its reason, and review it at the end.
Set a stopping point before you start, and stop there.

constraints.text: Every input accepts values pasted from a spreadsheet.
Lines of text no longer than 70 characters.

tasks.text: Churn cost calculator: customer count, monthly loss rate, and average value per customer give the revenue lost each year and what a one-point cut would keep.
Discount impact calculator: list price, margin, and discount percent give the extra sales needed to keep the same profit, with each step shown.
Error cost estimator: cases per month, error rate, and cost to fix each give the monthly cost of mistakes and the saving at half the error rate.
Stakeholder map: the people a change affects, rated by influence and support, give a two-by-two grid and the person to talk to first.
Contract term comparer: monthly and yearly prices for the same service give the total over 12, 24, and 36 months and the cheaper term for each.
Seasonality planner: last year's monthly volumes give the peak and quiet months and the staff hours each month needs.

temperaments.text: Repeats the other side's point back before answering.
Asks what would change their mind, then waits.
Brings a written list and works through it in order.
Goes quiet, then returns with a counter-example.

Argues the opposite side to test an idea.
methods: Design the error and empty states first.
List the assumptions in the brief and check each one.
Make it work in black and white before adding color.
Take the conventions of a genre and break exactly one.
Write the copy before the layout.
Scope the work to what fits in one day.
constraints: Under 100 words of fixed text on the page.
tasks: Cost-of-inaction calculator: the buyer's current volumes and rates give what the problem costs per month and per year, with each step of the sum shown.
Readiness scorecard: twelve yes-or-no questions give a score out of 100, the three weakest areas, and one next step for each.
Benchmark checker: the buyer's own figures sit next to typical ranges they can edit, with each gap marked ahead, level, or behind.
Leak finder: a funnel of stages with counts gives the stage that loses the most and what fixing half of that loss would be worth.
Time-back calculator: weekly hours on manual tasks and an hourly cost give the hours and money an automated step would return.
Before-and-after map: today's process as a list of steps becomes a side-by-side view marking the steps that could be removed or automated.
